entities.summary: Magnus Erikssons landslag, also known as simply the Landslagen, was a Swedish code of law passed by King Magnus Eriksson around 1341. It was the first attempt to apply a legal code to the entire nation of Sweden, replacing the previous local county laws under medieval Scandinavian law. The Country Law applied to the entire countryside, but not to the cities, which were governed according to the Stadslagen, which were issued in about the same time, but were separate. Kristofers landslag from 1442 was an amended version this law, in effect in Sweden until the Civil Code of 1734.
